title: A Noisy Evening
instructions: Listen carefully. Choose the option that best matches what is said or implied.

audio.description: Flatmates discuss a considerate way to handle evening noise.

transcript.text: The music next door was loud after eleven last night. I have an early shift, but do not want an argument over one evening.
It has happened three times this month. A polite note asking them to lower it after ten may help; they may not know how far sound carries.
A note is a good start. If it happens again, I would speak the next morning, when everyone is calmer.
Agreed. Let’s mention thin walls and politely ask them to lower the music at night.
I can write it today. If it continues, we can check the building guidance and decide what to do next.

questions.prompt: Why is Flatmate A reluctant to act immediately?
options: They do not have an early shift.
They do not want to cause an argument over one evening.
questions.explanation: They say they do not want to start an argument over one evening, despite having an early shift.

questions.prompt: Why does Flatmate B suggest leaving a note?
options: The neighbours have asked for written feedback.
They cannot speak to anyone in the building.
The neighbours may not know how much sound travels.
The music has already stopped permanently.
questions.explanation: They suggest the neighbours might not realise how clearly the sound carries.

questions.prompt: Why would Flatmate A wait until the next morning to speak?
options: People may be less annoyed then.
The building is closed at night.
The music is only loud in the morning.
They need permission from the owner first.
questions.explanation: They say speaking the next morning may be better than knocking while everyone is annoyed.

questions.prompt: What tone do they want the note to have?
questions.explanation: They agree to avoid making it sound like a formal complaint and ask politely.
